parsed.study_design: Longitudinal utility-level panel study using fixed-effects and dynamic panel models
parsed.population_and_sample: 208 large and medium urban water utilities in 192 prefecture-level cities, observed from 1998 to 2007; city-level service analyses included up to 814 observations.
parsed.exposure: Private-sector participation in utility ownership, defined by nonstate capital and distinguished as majority versus minority private shareholding.
parsed.outcome: Urban water-supply volume, domestic water-supply volume, number of domestic water users, and utility performance indicators including employment, expenses, profitability, investment, and productivity.
parsed.rationale: Section III (pp. 160–163) identifies the longitudinal sample, ownership exposure, and measured utility and city-level outcomes. Section V.D and Table 8 (pp. 181–184) empirically estimate the effects of private-sector participation on domestic water-supply population and water-supply volumes, including evidence of increased domestic users under majority private participation. This directly links an institutional-governance factor to household water-service coverage/access outcomes.
